MN202611_15674ts01am.t:
The future of Poundland hangs in the balance as it faces a possible collapse into administration.

Its owner, US investment firm Gordon Brothers, put it up for sale in September, but then rejected offers to keep the business afloat.

Poundland has a major presence on the High Street, with 600 stores in the UK and Ireland, where it trades under the Dealz brand.

If it were to collapse, the jobs of its 11,000 employees would be at risk, as well as potentially thousands of others at firms that supply the retailer.

People have not stopped shopping at Poundland - quite the opposite.

Although the chain was struggling when it was sold by Pepco last year for £1, the business turned a corner over the year to September, going from a £68m loss to an £18.1m profit before interest, tax and certain accounting charges.

Going into the vital Christmas period, first-quarter like-for-like sales were up 7% and operational profits of £1.9m were up £1.2m on last year.

Halloween sales were 11.4% higher than last year - this is usually a good indicator of how a retailer will do at Christmas, says retail analyst Catherine Shuttleworth of Savvy Marketing.

According to Julie Palmer, managing partner at insolvency specialist Begbies Traynor: "This isn't a story about shoppers abandoning Poundland. The tills are busier than they were a year ago."

She adds: "On the face of it, a turnaround seems well under way."

However, Gordon Brothers has been restricting Poundland's access to cash needed to restock stores and meet day-to-day expenses.

It had frozen about £50m in funds leading to concerns Poundland's shops would run out of stock.

However, Gordon Brothers released around £21m over two weeks recently, giving the chain a little more breathing space.

Poundland seems to be facing "a funding and ownership problem rather than a trading collapse", Palmer says.

However, while Poundland boss Barry Williams says the business is making a "strong recovery", Gordon Brothers has painted a different picture, saying the chain remains "challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading".

It says it has provided significant funding to support the company's ability to trade since it acquired the business.

It has also made about £18m from a combination of debt interest payments and other fees and charges.

As well as being Poundland's owner, it is one of its lenders, and is owed loans, including a £22.5m shareholder loan it inherited when it bought the business for £1.

As the main creditor, Gordon Brothers would be first in line to get paid back if the business goes under - but its suppliers are not.

"When the owner is also the main lender, its first priority is recovering [loans]," says Palmer. "Sometimes the route that best protects the lender is different from the one that saves the most jobs, and that tension is why this has become such a political story."

Irish firm Martin Property Group has offered to buy the business as a going concern, while London-based holding company Xyra Group has also made a rescue bid , although doubts remain about the credibility of Xyra's offer.

There is also a third, unnamed bid on the table.

Gordon Brothers has also been weighing options to break Poundland up.

The US company's view is that ultimately breaking the retailer up will provide more security for employees in the long term, because any buyers of its store estate will also have to agree to keep the employees on.

Insiders who are critical of how Gordon Brothers has handled the Poundland sale say it is driving the business into the ground to make money through the insolvency process.

But the investment firm, which specialises in buying and restructuring distressed companies, has denied the claim.

For now, Poundland has avoided immediate collapse after a deadline was extended by 10 days to find a rescue deal .

Shuttleworth says the future of Poundland is "really unclear, with the owners and the management at loggerheads about its future".

Palmer says there are two ways forward for Poundland - either a solvent deal, where the company gets bought and carries on trading, or a collapse followed by a break-up.

"The immediate make-or-break issue is Christmas: a value retailer that can't get stock on its shelves in November and December is in serious trouble, whatever its full-year results say," says Palmer.

There has been political pressure on Gordon Brothers from both Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds. They have called for answers over why the Martin Property Group offer to buy the business, which would have protected jobs, was rejected.

A committee of MPs also questioned Gordon Brothers last week, adding to pressure.

But Shuttleworth says that as a US firm Gordon Brothers appears "unmoved" by the arguments that the UK government has put forward.

MN202611_pmz87xs4or.t:
The city of San Francisco is the heart of the AI sector

Lauren Goldboss is busy. The owner of a small San Francisco dog-walking company, she has been hiring staff and buying vans.

Fuelling the growth is her new office dog-walking service Paw Perk, popular with some local AI start-ups.

Her business is an example of how the AI boom in San Francisco is benefiting other sectors.

The city saw an exodus of residents during the pandemic and its downtown was weakened by remote work, but it s now enjoying a rejuvenation, with AI being the major driver.

Lauren Goldboss walks dogs for AI workers

Leading AI firms OpenAI and Anthropic – which have been hiring top engineering talent, often on eye-popping salaries – are based here. Anthropic, the company behind the Claude chatbot, last week listed on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange.

Thousands of other AI start-ups have also sprung up , external in San Francisco.

Signs of the boom are evident in soaring rents and house prices, falling office vacancies, and buses and billboards plastered with cryptic AI adverts.

But what if there is a significant downward correction in AI share prices and a resulting big fall in investment in the industry? The International Monetary Fund last month became the latest organization to warn , external that this was a possibility.

Concerns have since continued due to the scandal surrounding Jensen Huang, the former boss of AI firm Nvidia, based south of San Francisco, causing some wider AI stock falls. However, Nvidia remains highly profitable, and Wednesday of this week it reported that its latest quarterly profits had doubled from a year earlier to $65bn (£49bn).

Simon Jack: Can Anthropic's record-breaking IPO stop the AI bubble bursting?

The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal

Wealthy AI workers send San Francisco house prices soaring

Follow the money: Who pays for the AI boom now?

What are the thoughts of AI workers in the city, and should San Francisco – no stranger to tech's boom-and-bust cycles – be preparing for a possible crash?

One AI worker, employed by one of the largest companies in the city, is convinced that a crash is coming. "I am certain that the house of cards will come down… and I'm sure it will affect me," says the man who asked that we didn't use his name.

He questions whether leading US AI companies can generate enough revenues to justify their enormous spending commitments as cheaper, increasingly capable AI models emerge, especially from China.

But he isn't losing sleep over it. "Why worry about things I can't control?"

Another San Francisco-based AI worker, who also asked to remain anonymous, says that a significant market correction is "totally possible".

Yet he adds that most people don't think of it as the core risk. Instead, he says that the bigger concern in his circles, and the one he shares, is the existential risk that AI could pose to humanity.

"In some weird way, a market correction being the worst-case outcome feels great."

If there is an AI crash, San Francisco could be hit far more than Silicon Valley which lies 40 miles to its south.

That's because the AI boom is very much centred on the city itself rather than the wider San Francisco Bay Area, which includes Silicon Valley.

One study , external found that 60% of all venture capital invested in US AI firms from 2023 to 2025 went to the companies located in San Francisco, dwarfing the significantly smaller percentage given to companies in Silicon Valley.

But some factors suggest that the impact of a crash in San Francisco may be softer than some fear.

For all the investment they have attracted, AI companies are employing relatively few workers in the city compared to previous tech booms. So there may not be that many jobs to lose in a downturn.

"Hiring isn't necessarily on the scale as we would have thought with the amount of venture capital and new company formation," says Jeff Bellisario, executive director of the Bay Area Council Economic Institute, a business-affiliated think tank.

Ted Egan, the chief economist for the City and County of San Francisco, adds that "because of AI, it is a good time for tech again in the city, but we are not seeing tonnes of overall tech job growth".

Despite the expansion of the AI sector, the city remains about 35,000 jobs shy of its pre-pandemic peak, estimates Enrico Moretti, an economics professor at the University of California, Berkeley.

Instead, much of the spending by AI firms in the US is going towards data centres and computing power, relatively little of which are located in the Bay Area. San Francisco might be the brains of the AI boom, but it isn't the brawn.

Nonetheless, a significant correction could still be "very painful" for San Francisco, warns Moretti. Less AI hiring and potential layoffs would ripple through the local service sector, likely to affect jobs in everything from restaurants, to retail, to personal services like dog walking.

"It is the spillover on service jobs that would actually be the main effect," he says.

Office vacancies could also rise, reducing downtown foot traffic, while rents and house prices could weaken.

Huge data centres are being built across the US to power AI

But AI isn't the only force driving San Francisco's recovery. Healthcare and tourism – which the city has been working to encourage, including by improving downtown safety and cleanliness – are also growing, , external which may help cushion against a possible AI downturn.

"Tourism is not fully back, but the growth has been healthy," says Egan, adding that it is a sign of confidence in San Francisco.

All told, Egan doesn't expect an AI crash to fundamentally alter San Francisco's economic trajectory.

"The city's economy has not been screaming during this AI boom, so I wouldn't expect it to grind to a halt if there was a slowdown in AI spending," he says. "I think of it primarily as a hiccup that we should expect, rather than a major course correction for the city's economy."

As to whether and how San Francisco's city government should prepare, there are limits to what it can do, note Bellisario and Moretti. But encouraging growth in sectors beyond technology and maintaining financial reserves could help.

For Goldboss, the dog-walking company owner, her philosophy is to "build while it is here". If the next tech bust comes – "always a reality in San Francisco" – she will try to adapt to what the market needs. "It is just the risk you kind of have to take," she says.

MN202611_1dt5tu0xy3q.t:
Keeping yourself warm by wearing thick clothes, using blankets and having hot drinks can help reduce heating bills

Energy prices are forecast to rise by 26% for millions of homes in January, but experts say there are ways to keep a check on rising bills.

Here are four areas to consider ahead of the increase.

Energy regulator Ofgem's price cap, as well as suppliers' fixed deals, set a limit on the price of each unit of energy, not the total bill.

So, you pay for what you use. Millions of people have cut back on their energy consumption during years of relatively high prices.

With the unit price of gas, in particular, set to soar, experts say you should take a fresh look at your energy use and renew good habits.

turning down the flow temperature on a combi boiler - usually indicated by a radiator icon, to make it operate more efficiently

turning off the pre-heat facility on some combi boilers, which would have kept some water heated up when not in use

turning down the thermostat one degree, although 18C is the recommended minimum

lowering radiator valves outside of the living room

These are small changes but - alongside washing clothes at 30C, blocking draughts and batch cooking - they can reduce energy use and bills.

Ofgem says about five million people still pay their bill when it arrives every three months, rather than receive a monthly bill often initially based on an estimate.

Taking regular meter readings, or having a smart meter, while paying by monthly direct debit solves that problem.

Paying by direct debit costs significantly less than by so-called standard credit - typically £138 cheaper a year.

Customers on prepayment schemes - usually people on low incomes struggling to pay bills - used to pay a higher rate than others, but now they pay slightly less than the capped direct debit variable rate.

Various deals may rely on paying by direct debit or having a smart meter.

Moving to a fixed energy tariff means the price you are charged per unit of gas or electricity does not change every three months, although the total bill will still vary depending on how much energy you use.

The trouble is that it is very difficult to work out whether a fixed deal is a good deal at the moment, for those renewing fixed deals or looking for one for the first time.

Some fixed deals are available at unit prices below the next forecast price cap level. But should energy prices fall sharply then a longer-term fix might not seem such good value compared with the price cap.

So consumer group Which? also recommends paying close attention to any exit fees when picking a fixed deal. If variable prices fall below your fixed rate and you want to get out of it before the end of your agreement period, you may have to pay a hefty sum.

Before you fix, consumer website MoneySavingExpert advises you look at all the deals available , not just what your own supplier is offering.

The government will give a £100 payment to millions of homes to help cover winter energy costs. It will go to homes in council tax bands A to D in England, with the equivalent expected in Scotland and Wales.

There are also a range of other forms of support specifically for people on low incomes .

This winter anyone on means-tested benefits will get £150 off their electricity bill.

Your supplier will apply the discount automatically unless you are in Scotland, where you will need to contact your energy company to ask for the help.

Some people will also be eligible for a Cold Weather Payment , external and most pensioners will receive the winter fuel payment.

Beyond that, most energy suppliers offer hardship grants for people struggling to pay their bills and the government's Fuel Direct Scheme , external can help you repay energy debt.

You can get more advice from Ofgem , external , Citizens Advice , external , or your own energy supplier. Trade body Energy UK has a list of support schemes , external .

People on low incomes may also be eligible for grants to help with insulating their homes, and there are local schemes offering grants for solar panels, heat pumps and the like.

But if you are hunting around for grants, watch out for scams pretending to be official money-off schemes.

MN202611_ddod7amt5.t:
The trial will assess if AI can improve breast cancer diagnosis

Nearly 700,000 women across the UK are to be invited to join the world's largest trial of how artificial intelligence can help in breast cancer screening.

AI will be used to review mammograms to see if it can improve early cancer detection and ease the workload of clinical staff, while not over-diagnosing women unnecessarily.

Recruitment to the EDITH trial , external has already begun at Cambridge University Hospitals, the first of 30 sites across the UK.

Women aged 50 to 71 are invited for routine breast screening every three years in the UK, and more than two million attend annually.

At present two NHS experts look at each breast X-ray, known as a mammogram, but in the trial, one of the human readers will be replaced by AI.

Several smaller studies have already shown that AI can improve breast cancer detection rates, but researchers running this trial say they need to be sure it won't cause harm by leading to women being recalled unnecessarily for further tests.

Sian Taylor-Phillips, professor of population health at the University of Warwick, and co-chief investigator said: "AI-assisted technology could help improve early cancer detection but we want to avoid the overdiagnosis of milder disease that would never have caused symptoms."

Breast cancer is the most common cancer among women in the UK, with around 59,000 cases diagnosed each year.

About a third of these are picked up by routine mammograms, usually at an early stage when they can be more easily treated.

It's estimated the screening programme helps prevent around 1,300 deaths a year.

Shirley Essex says routine breast screening saved her life

Prof Fiona Gilbert, department of radiology, University of Cambridge, honorary consultant at Addenbrooke's Hospital, and co-chief investigator said: "Millions of women have a mammogram each year and only a small number, less than 1%, will have cancer.

"Technology can make reviewing these images more efficient, freeing up specialist breast radiologists to spend more time caring for patients with cancer, supporting faster diagnosis and earlier treatment."

Gilbert told the BBC there was a "huge shortfall" in radiologists and that the number of imaging examinations was increasing by 8% a year.

Shirley Essex, 70, from Cambridgeshire, was diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer a year ago after a routine screening appointment.

She had surgery and radiotherapy, but did not require chemotherapy.

She told the BBC that her mammogram had saved her life: "I was astonished to be told I had cancer because I did not have any symptoms."

Shirley is not part of the study but is passionate about the importance of screening.

"I feel so lucky my cancer was detected early. It was my last routine mammogram, so if I had not attended, my cancer would have kept growing," she said.

Women will be informed about the study when they receive a routine screening invitation, but will not be obliged to take part.

The trial will not change what happens during a breast screening appointment.

Instead, it will test whether AI-assisted tools could replace one of the two human specialists reviewing mammograms.

Researchers say machine-learning software can be trained on millions of previous images in order to detect patterns, and so potentially find subtle changes in breast tissue that might be missed by the human eye.

In one arm of the trial, an AI programme will grade images before they are sent to NHS experts. In another, it will review images afterwards.

The £11m trial is funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR).

It is being led by the University of Warwick, the University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, working with NHS England.

On a visit to the breast screening unit at Addenbrooke's Hospital, Health Secretary Yvette Cooper told the BBC: "AI has huge potential to improve treatment, which is why we need trials like this to ensure we are using it in the most effective way with proper safeguards."

Prof Peter Johnson, national clinical director for cancer at NHS England, said NHS breast screening "saves lives" and he urged every woman invited to the trial to take part.

"Every scan will still be seen by a specialist, and if proven effective, it could ensure women get the diagnosis and treatment they need sooner," he said.

Four AI companies are involved in the trial, which is expected to last around three years.

MN202611_3ptmkb1ftl.t:
Umuhanzi Nyarwanda Kwizera Emmanuel Prince uzwi nka Run Up, yegukanye igihembo cy’indirimbo ifite amashusho meza yo muri Afurika (Best African Music Video) mu bihembo bya Galsen Urban Awards byabaye ku nshuro ya 12, abikesha indirimbo ye yitwa “Que Paso”.

Ibi bihembo byatangiwe i Dakar muri Sénégal, mu ijoro ryo ku wa Gatandatu, tariki ya 21 Ugushyingo 2026.

Nk’uko byatangajwe na Ambasade y’u Rwanda muri Sénégal, igikombe RunUp yegukanye cyashyikirijwe Ambasade y’u Rwanda muri icyo gihugu, kugira ngo izagishyikirize uyu muhanzi.

Uretse RunUp, undi muhanzi Nyarwanda, Ish Kevin, yari mu bahataniye igihembo cy’umuhanzi mwiza muri Afurika (Best African Artist), bigaragaza ko abahanzi Nyarwanda bakomeje kumenyekana no guhatanira ibihembo ku rwego rw’umugabane wa Afurika.

Galsen Urban Awards ni ibihembo bihuriza hamwe abahanzi bakora umuziki ugezweho baturutse mu bihugu bitandukanye bya Afurika. Bigamije gushimira impano z’abahanzi, guteza imbere imikoranire mu muziki no kwimakaza amahoro, ubumwe no guhererekanya umuco.

Ambasade y’u Rwanda muri Sénégal yashimiye RunUp, itsinda ryamufashije gutunganya amashusho y’indirimbo “Que Paso” ndetse na Ish Kevin, igaragaza ko ibyo bagezeho ari ishema ku Rwanda kandi bigaragaza ubushobozi bw’impano nyafurika bwo kurenga imipaka no guhuza abantu.

Umuhanzi RunUp yatangiye umuziki akiri muto, aza gushyira hanze indirimbo zirimo nka "Isabella", "Flower", na "DELETE" mu mwaka wa 2023.

Yagize izina rikomeye mu muziki Nyarwanda kuva mu 2024 abikesheje indirimbo "On God" yakoranye n'umuhanzi Pallaso wo muri Uganda, ndetse n'indirimbo "See". Yamenyekanye cyane kandi mu ndirimbo nka "Tsunami" anavuga ko yahinduye amateka ye mu muziki, hamwe na "Que Paso" yasohotse muri 2026 ari na yo yegukanye igihembo.

MN202611_8apuwvirdp.t:
'Danger seems greater all the time': Ukrainians search for missing after Russian strikes hit Kyiv

A seven-year-old boy has been rescued from the rubble of a residential building in Dymer after 14 hours, in overnight Russian strikes on Dymer, in the Kyiv region, that killed nine people, Ukrainian officials have said.

The attack occurred in the early hours of Sunday. A 79-year-old woman was also rescued alive from the collapsed building, Kyiv's regional head Tymur Tkachenko said.

A strike on a private home in Bila Tserkva killed one more person and set the building ablaze, he added.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky also said three people were killed and 13 wounded in a separate strike on Vyshneve, also in the Kyiv region, that hit a grocery store on Sunday.

Ukrainian authorities said the boy in Dymer is in stable condition and was taken to hospital, and have thanked everyone involved in saving his life.

Zelensky and Ukraine's national police also confirmed the rescue of the boy.

Response teams including police, explosive technicians, dog handlers and medics are continuing with rescue efforts.

In a telegram post, Tkachenko said the 79-year-old woman rescued from the rubble was receiving treatment in hospital.

Earlier he said six people were injured in the attack, while others were still missing.

The attack on the residential building occurred in the early hours of the morning while people were asleep

Zelensky said more than 130 people are involved in emergency operations at the scene, and that they will continue until they have "complete information about every single person".

Sending his condolences to the families and loved ones of those killed, he said the strike struck the residential building, "practically blowing a section of it to smithereens".

Zelensky added that "rescue efforts are complicated by constant new air raid alerts and renewed threats".

The strike hit the building at 05:00 local time, when families were still asleep, Ukraine's minister of internal affairs Ivan Vyhivskyi said.

More than 70 strikes have been launched across 10 Ukrainian regions as of Sunday evening, Vyhivskyi added.

Emergency workers continue to search for those missing after Russian drone and missile attacks in Dymer.

In his video address posted online, Zelensky also said three people were killed and 13 injured in a strike on an "ordinary grocery store" in Vyshneve.

Tkachenko previously said two other people were killed and eight wounded in the Vyshneve attack.

Russia also struck a power substation in the Dnipropetrovsk region, Ukraine's Prime Minister Sergiy Koretsky said in a post on X. , external

MN202611_map8uolvxq.t: Ubwato bw’intambara bw’Uburusiya bwari buhagaze ku kivuko ca Benghazi mu buseruko bwa Libya bwononekaye cane mu gitero abategetsi bavuga ko gishobora kuba cakozwe n’indege itajamwo umudereva (drone). Reta igenzura ubuseruko bwa Libya yatangaje ko ibiturika vyumvikanye ejo ku wa Mungu ku bwato bw’Uburusiya bwari ku kigo c’ingabo zo mu mazi hafi ya Benghazi. Amafoto yafashwe n’ibigendajuru yerekana ko ubwo bwato bwahengamye cane kandi buri hafi yo kwibira, hasigaye igice c’imbere gusa kigaragara hejuru y’amazi. Ubwo bwato bwamenyekanye kw’izina rya Merkury, Ubwato buto bw’intambara bufitaniye isano n’amato y’intambara y’Uburusiya akorera mu Kiyaga Cirabura. Abategetsi ba Libya bavuga ko bwari bwahagaze i Benghazi kugira bunywe igitoro bwongere bupakire imizigo hanyuma busubire mu Burusiya. Abategetsi bakeka ko muri ico gitero hakoreshejwe amadrone yo mu mazi yari atekeye ibiturika, ariko nta ruhande na rumwe ruraciyitirira. Uburusiya na bwo nyene ntiburagira ico bubivugako. Amakuru ava mu buvuzi avuga ko ata wapfuye muri ico gitero, ariko ko abantu nka 10 bahakomerekeye. Mu kindi gitero cabaye ejo nyene, ubwato bw’ubudandaji bufise ibendera rya Malte na bwo bwaratewe hafi y’inkombe za Benghazi. Abategetsi bavuga ko abasare bose barokowe n’ingabo za Libya zirwanira mu mazi. Ibinyamakuru vyo muri Libya vyavuze ko inzego z’umutekano zasamiye mu kirere amadrone ashika 12 yari atekeye ibiturika hejuru ya Benghazi mu gihe haba ivyo bitero. Ubutegetsi bwo mu buseruko bwa Libya bwateye ivyatsi ivyo bitero, ivuga ko bihonyanga ubugusire n’umutekano wo mu mazi vy’ico gihugu, bushimangira kandi ko Libya idakwiye guhinduka urwasiro rw’intambara mvamahanga. Abategetsi kandi bashimangira ko Libya ata ruhande urwo ari rwo rwose yegamiye mu ntambara hagati y’Uburusiya na Ukraine. Ntibatangaje uwoba ari inyuma y’ivyo bitero, ariko amakuru avuga ko abahinga ba Ukraine mu gukoresha no kuyobora amadrone bariko bakorera mu buseruko bwa Libya. Ayandi makuru ushobora gusoma: Zelensky avuga ko Putin ari 'umwicanyi' nyuma yuko Trump yise Perezida w'Uburusiya inshuti Ubwato bwajyaga mu Burusiya buracyari gushya nyuma y'igitero bwagabweho mu kigobe cya Finland Zelensky avuga ko kurasa iteme rya Crimea byari 'igisubizo kiboneye', mu gihe yahuraga na Minisitiri w'ingabo w'Ubwongereza

Muri weekend dushoje Minisiteri y'Ubuzima yatangiye gushyira mu bikorwa ivugurura rya serivisi z’ubutabazi bwihuse mu buvuzi (Rwanda Emergency Medical Services – EMS), rigamije kunoza uburyo abarwayi n’abakeneye ubutabazi bwihuse bagerwaho n’izo serivisi mu gihugu hose.

Iri vugurura ryatangijwe mu cy’igikorwa cya Siporo rusange (Car Free Day) ku cyumweru tariki 22 Ugushyingo 2026, rikaba rigamije kubaka uburyo bwihuse kandi bwihariye bwo gutanga ubutabazi, bushingiye ku iterambere u Rwanda rumaze kugeraho muri uru rwego.

Mu ntego Minisiteri yihaye kugeraho muri iri vugurura kugeraho mu 2030, harimo kugabanya igihe imodoka z’imbangukiragutabara zimara zigera ku muntu ukeneye ubutabazi, ku buryo mu Mujyi wa Kigali zizajya zihagera mu minota 10 ugereranyije, mu gihe mu tundi turere zizajya zihagera mu minota 20.

Rinateganya ko hazaba hari imodoka imwe y’imbangukiragutabara nibura ku bantu ibihumbi 20, hagashyirwaho n’ubundi buryo bwihariye bwo gutanga ubutabazi burimo imodoka zagenewe impinja zikivuka, abarwayi bafite indwara zandura ndetse n’izagenewe gutwara abantu benshi.

Uretse imodoka zisanzwe, hazanifashishwa kandi amapikipiki, ubwato n’indege mu kugeza ubutabazi ku bantu, bitewe n’aho baherereye n’ubwoko bw’ubufasha bakeneye.

Mu rwego rwo kongerera ubushobozi abatanga ubu butabazi, u Rwanda rurateganya gufungura ishuri rya mbere ryigisha umwuga w’ubutabazi bwihuse (Paramedic School), rikazajya ryakira abanyeshuri 100 buri mwaka biga ku rwego rwa dipolome.

Ikoranabuhanga na ryo rizagira uruhare muri iri vugurura, aho hazakoreshwa uburyo bwa GPS butuma imodoka z’imbangukiragutabara zikurikiranwa mu gihe nyacyo binyuze muri sisitemu ya eBanguka, ndetse n’ikoranabuhanga ry’ubwenge buhangano (AI) rifasha mu gufata ibyemezo bijyanye n’ubutabazi.

Ikindi ni uko abakozi bo mu bigo nderabuzima n’ibitaro 69 bazahabwa amahugurwa ku buryo bw’ibanze bwo gutanga ubutabazi bwihuse, azwi nka WHO Basic Emergency Care.

Iri vugurura rinateganya guhugura abantu 2.000 bazajya batanga ubutabazi bw’ibanze mu baturage, kuko ari bo bafatwa nk’intambwe ya mbere mu ruhererekane rwo kurokora ubuzima bw’umuntu uri mu kaga.

Amahugurwa azaherwa mu Mujyi wa Kigali, aho azahabwa abapolisi, abamotari n’abacuruzi bo mu masoko, kugira ngo bashobore gutanga ubufasha bw’ibanze mu gihe bahuye n’umuntu ukeneye ubutabazi bwihuse, batarategereza ko abakozi b’ubuvuzi bahagera.

Ibi bishimangira ko gutanga ubutabazi bwihuse bidakwiye kugarukira ku bitaro gusa, ahubwo bigomba gutangirira hafi y’umuturage, kugira ngo umuntu ukeneye ubufasha abubone hakiri kare.

Minisitiri w’Umutekano w’Imbere mu Gihugu, Dr Vincent Biruta, yitabiriye ibiganiro bitandukanye mu nama ya Aswan Forum iri kubera mu Misiri, aho yagarutse ku bibazo by’umutekano mu Karere k’Ibiyaga Bigari ndetse n’uburyo bwo guhangana n’ikibazo cy’abakurwa mu byabo n’intambara n’ibindi bibazo.

Ku munsi wa mbere w’iyi nama, Minisitiri Biruta yitabiriye ikiganiro cyibanze ku kubaka amahoro arambye mu Karere k’Ibiyaga Bigari cyari gifite insangamatsiko igira iti: “Building Sustainable Peace in the Great Lakes Region”.

Muri icyo kiganiro, yashimangiye ko kugira ngo amakimbirane akomeje kugaragara mu Burasirazuba bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo (RDC) abonerwe umuti urambye, hakenewe gukemura ibiyateza, birimo ikibazo cy’umutwe wa FDLR, ugizwe n’abasize bakoze Jenoside yakorewe Abatutsi mu 1994.

Yasabye kandi impande zose zifitanye isano n’amasezerano ya Washington agamije mahoro kubahiriza ibyo ziyemeje, agaragaza ko ayo masezerano azatanga umusaruro ari uko buri ruhande rushyize mu bikorwa inshingano zarwo, ndetse n’ubuhuza bukorwa mu buryo butabogamye.

Ku munsi wa kabiri w’iyi nama, Minisitiri Biruta yitabiriye kandi n'ikiganiro cyari gifite insangamatsiko igira iti: “Beyond Borders and Responsibility Sharing: The Unresolved Challenge of Forced Displacement”, cyibanze ku kibazo cyabava mu byabo ku gahato n’inshingano ibihugu bifite zo gufatanya mu kugishakira ibisubizo, kikaba ari ikibazo gikomeje kubura umuti urambye.

Yagaragaje ubunararibonye bw’u Rwanda mu kwakira no gucunga impunzi n’abasaba ubuhungiro, anagaragaza ibisubizo bishya Igihugu kiri gukorana n’ibihugu by’i Burayi n’imiryango mpuzamahanga mu guhangana n’abimukira binjira cyangwa bagenda mu buryo budakurikije amategeko.

Ibi biganiro byibanze ku gushaka uburyo ibihugu n’imiryango mpuzamahanga byafatanya mu gukemura ibibazo by’abakurwa mu byabo n’intambara, kurinda uburenganzira bwabo no gushyiraho ibisubizo birambye kuri icyo kibazo.

Aswan Forum for Sustainable Peace and Development in Africa, ni inama mpuzamahanga ihuriza hamwe abayobozi, abahanga n’abafatanyabikorwa batandukanye kugira ngo baganire ku bibazo by’amahoro, umutekano n’iterambere rirambye muri Afurika.
